states.name: after_check_1
states.description: A Three.js WebGL renderer and scene are initialized and the canvas is present in the DOM

states.name: after_check_2
states.description: A central pool object is loaded into the scene and visible at the origin area

states.name: after_check_3
states.description: At least one CommercialRefrigerator model can be placed into the scene via the placement interaction

states.name: after_check_4
states.description: A total energy budget is defined and a UI element displays the current energy consumption vs the maximum budget

states.name: after_check_5
states.description: Placing a refrigerator increases the current energy consumption and the value is reflected in the UI

states.name: after_check_6
states.description: Placement is blocked or a warning is shown when adding a refrigerator would exceed the total energy budget

states.name: after_check_7
states.description: Each refrigerator has a cooling-efficiency modifier that varies based on its distance to the pool center — closer means higher efficiency

states.name: after_check_8
states.description: A refrigerator can be selected and rotated, and its rotation quaternion changes after the interaction

states.name: after_check_9
states.description: A selected refrigerator can be deleted from the scene and the energy consumption decreases accordingly

states.name: after_check_10
states.description: An undo stack exists and calling undo after a placement action removes the last placed refrigerator and restores energy

states.name: after_check_11
states.description: A redo stack exists and calling redo after an undo restores the previously undone action

states.name: after_check_12
states.description: Undo/redo supports all three action types: placement, rotation, and deletion — the undo stack entries carry an action type field
